Series::expm1¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::expm1() const -> Series
Series& Series::expm1_()

What It Does¶

expm1() applies e^x - 1 elementwise.

Mathematically, that is the same quantity you would get from exp(x) - 1, but it is exposed as its own method because it is a common transform in its own right, especially around values close to zero.

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

Series A new Series with the same shape as self, containing e^x - 1 lane by lane.

Gradient¶

If y = e^x - 1, then:

  • dy/dx = e^x

  • equivalently, dy/dx = y + 1

So when the objective is L = sum(y), each lane contributes its own e^{x_i} as the local backward multiplier.

In-Place Form¶

expm1_() is the in-place sibling of expm1(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

auto x = pluss::make_series({0.0, 1.0});

auto& ref = x.expm1_();
std::cout << "x=" << x << "\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "same object: " << (&ref == &x);

Output¶

x=pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 1.7182818]
same object: true

Examples¶

Example 1. The transform preserves shape and shifts the ordinary exponential down by one.

std::cout << pluss::series::print(pluss::make_series({-1.0, 0.0, 1.0}).expm1());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.6321, 0.0000, 1.7183]

Example 2. Reverse-mode multiplies by e^x, not by e^x - 1.

auto x = pluss::make_series({-1.0, 0.0, 1.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

auto y = x.expm1();
y.sum().reverse();

std::cout << "out=" << y << "\n";
std::cout << "dL_dx=" << x.sensitivity() << "\n";

Output¶

out=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.63212056, 0, 1.7182818]
dL_dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.36787944, 1, 2.7182818]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The returned values are e^x - 1, but the derivative is e^x.

  • Large positive inputs still grow quickly because this is still exponential.

  • Shape is preserved; there is no reduction, broadcasting, or axis toggle.

Summary¶

Use expm1() when the exact transform is “natural exponential, then subtract one” and you want that intent stated directly at the call site.

See Also¶

  • Series::exp: the unshifted natural exponential.

  • Series::log1p: the common logarithmic counterpart.
